title: fix(security,metadata-protocol): `deleteMany`'s per-row `success` stops reporting a deletion it did not perform
body:
Fixes #19412

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

Every row of `POST /api/v1/data/{object}/deleteMany` answered `success: true` for every engine
result that was not the driver contract's `false`. The `false` arm — "no row matched" — has
reported honestly since #4435. The other ending had not: a row that **MATCHED** and was
**deliberately NOT removed** was pushed as `success: true`, counted in `succeeded`, and shipped
an envelope byte-identical to a batch in which every id really went.

⚠️ This is the second half of one site, and the comment beside the loop is why it reads as
already fixed. That comment records the FIRST half — an earlier version "pushed `success: true`
unconditionally, so a batch of typo'd ids reported every one of them deleted" — which ADR-0119 D4
closed with the `deleted === false` throw. That throw answers **"there is no such record"**. It
says nothing about **"the record is right there and was not deleted"**, which is this card.

`sys_permission_set` is the shipped case: deleting a package-declared set is an ADR-0005 RESET —
plugin-security's write-through tombstones the overlay and the record re-projects to the declared
body instead of vanishing. The record surviving is the design. The answer was the defect, and on a
security-configuration write it tells an operator a permission set is gone while it is still being
enforced.

## Located by symbol, because the card's line numbers had already moved

The card cites `:13049` / `:13052` / `:13053`; the claim re-located them at `:13095` / `:13097` /
`:13098`. On this branch's base (`7ffddfa49`) they are:

| symbol | line on this base |
|:---|:---|
| `deleteManyData` | `:13026` |
| `runDeleteManyLoop` (where the defect actually lives — both arms share it) | `:13072` |
| `const deleted = await this.engine.delete(...)` | `:13094` |
| `if (deleted === false) throw recordNotFoundError(...)` | `:13097` |
| `results.push({ id: String(id), success: true, index })` | `:13098` |

## What `engine.delete` actually returns — measured, not assumed

`IDataEngine.delete` declares `Promise[boolean | number]` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts:279`;
square brackets here for a generic, the spelling that file's own contract test uses) — the driver
boolean for a by-id write, a COUNT of rows removed otherwise. `isDeleteResultShape`
(`packages/objectql/src/verb-hook-result-shape.ts:274`) is a pair of `typeof` tests, so a number is
admitted at this seam **today**.

Measured on this base with a fake engine per arm, both doors, before any edit:

| `engine.delete` answers | batch door, before | single door, on this base |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `true` | `success: true`, `succeeded: 1` | `{"success":true}` |
| `1` | `success: true`, `succeeded: 1` | `{"success":true}` |
| **`0`** | **`success: true`, `succeeded: 1`, `failed: 0`** | `{"success":true}` |
| `false` | `success: false` + `errors[0].code RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, `failed: 1` | throws `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |
| `undefined` | `success: true` | `{"success":true}` |

⇒ zero rows removed — the contract's one positive "it is still there" — was reported as a deletion.

## ⚠️ Where the tree disagrees with the card, and why the fix stands anyway

The card's mechanism is right and its **value** is not yet on the tree. On `origin/main` today the
permission-set write-through's delete leg is still `let lastOutcome: any = true` with its only
assignment `lastOutcome = res?.deleted ? true : lastOutcome`
(`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-projection.ts:1295`–`:1306`) — **no path to
any other value**. So a packaged set's reset answers this seam with `true`, not `0`, and *neither*
door can tell it from a real deletion on today's `main`.

The `0` arrives with PR #19411, which is OPEN and makes that leg report the count of records that
actually went. That PR then teaches the **single-record** door to read it. This branch teaches the
**batch** door to read it, and does not depend on #19411 having landed:

- the `number` arm is declared and admitted on this base, independently of any plugin;
- an `afterDelete` handler is explicitly allowed to reshape the result within that union
  (`DeleteHookResultNotWriteShapeError`'s own `developerMessage` says so), and a non-ObjectQL
  `IDataEngine` may answer with a count directly;
- the reset case is **reachable through this door**: the write-through is registered as an engine
  middleware scoped `{ object: 'sys_permission_set' }` (`security-plugin.ts:3459`), and
  `runDeleteManyLoop` calls the same `engine.delete` per id, so `deleteMany` traverses exactly the
  seam the by-id door traverses.

⇒ the two PRs are independent halves of one seam. Landing this one alone removes a lie the batch
door tells for any engine, middleware or handler that speaks the count arm; landing it beside
#19411 is what makes the packaged-set case honest at both doors.

## The fix

`runDeleteManyLoop`'s per-row push reads the engine result instead of being a literal:

```ts
const removed = deleted !== 0;
results.push({ id: String(id), success: removed, index });
if (removed) succeeded++;
else failed++;
```

⛔ **Not `false` for this case.** That arm is spoken for by the 404 above, about a record this
caller can still GET — answering it here would trade one wrong answer for a louder one. Only a
POSITIVE zero is read as "not removed"; an off-contract `undefined` from a third-party driver keeps
its #4435 reading.

## ⚠️ The single door's SHAPE transfers; its envelope does not come for free

`success: deleted !== 0` maps onto the row's `success` key verbatim — same declared meaning
("Whether this record was processed successfully"). Three things about the **batch** envelope had to
be decided separately, and they are the reason this is not a mirror:

1. **The row is counted in `failed`, and that is forced.** `reconcileStoppedBatch`'s contract text
   states the envelope's one reading: "`succeeded` and `failed` partition `results`, and
   `succeeded + failed === total === results.length`". A non-success row that is in neither bucket
   is the arithmetic mismatch #7539 exists to remove.
2. **So the request-level `success` goes false, and an `atomic` batch containing such a row now
   rolls back** — `runAtomicBatch` aborts on `outcome.failed > 0`. That follows mechanically from
   (1); it cannot be avoided while keeping the partition. Before this, an atomic `deleteMany`
   holding a packaged set committed and called every row deleted.
3. **A non-atomic batch is NOT stopped by it.** The `continueOnError` / `atomic` stop lives in the
   `catch`, and nothing is thrown — a surviving record is an outcome, not a fault. Every remaining
   id is still attempted, so the caller gets a complete per-row report.

⛔ **And the row gets no `errors[]` entry.** The single-record door answers this same case with a
bare `success: false` on a 200; the two per-row codes this envelope owns — `ROLLED_BACK` and
`NOT_ATTEMPTED` — both describe a row that never ran, and no registered code means "matched and
deliberately not deleted". Minting one is an `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` widening in `packages/spec`, which
belongs to the spec lane, exactly as #19411 left the `/meta` door's `reset` discriminator there.
Noted below rather than smuggled in here.

## On the wire, per row

| case | before | after |
|:---|:---|:---|
| row removed | `success: true`, in `succeeded` | unchanged |
| matched, not removed (packaged set reset) | `success: true`, in `succeeded` | `success: false`, in `failed`, no `errors[]` |
| unknown id | `success: false`, `errors[0].code RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | unchanged |
| batch stopped / rolled back | `NOT_ATTEMPTED` / `ROLLED_BACK` | unchanged |

HTTP status is untouched: the route is `res.json(result)` (`rest-server.ts:13867`), so this stays a
200 whose body reports per row — the same place a partially-failed batch has always reported.

## Evidence

All readings at `42a38d20c`, worktree clean, base `7ffddfa49`.

**The pin, and that it can fail.** `protocol.record-not-found.test.ts` gains three cases in the
`deleteManyData` block: the NEGATIVE case (engine answers `0` ⇒ `success: false`, `succeeded: 0`,
`failed: 1`, and **no** `errors` key, so a surviving record is never read as one that was never
there), a control leg (a positive count still reports a deletion), and a mixed batch that pins both
directions in one run. Run against the UNFIXED base first: **2 failed / 14 passed**. After the fix:
**16 passed**.

**Reverse verification**, both legs from the committed state, mutation proven on disk and restored
by blob hash (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`):

| mutation | anchor | blob | result |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| the four fixed lines back to `success: true` + `succeeded++` | x1 to x0 | `5a5572348e9b` to `9e18ad2bd75c` | **2 failed / 14 passed** |
| `const removed = deleted !== 0` to `const removed = false` | x1 to x0 | `5a5572348e9b` to `8e200f823448` | **4 failed / 12 passed** |

Both restored: blob equals `HEAD`'s (`5a5572348e9b`), `git diff HEAD` empty. ⚠️ The first attempt at
the first leg measured NOTHING and is reported as such: an `EXIT` trap in the calling shell restored
the file before vitest ran, so that run's green was a no-op. It was re-taken with the mutation and
the command in one process, which is the reading above. That red also proves the suite resolves
`src/protocol.ts` and not `dist/` — `dist/` held the FIXED bytes at that moment and the run still
went red.

**Unit + types.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` — **183 files (3 skipped) /
2615 passed (19 skipped)**, exit 0. `typecheck` exit 0, and `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` names
`protocol.record-not-found.test.ts`, so the pin is inside the program the script advertises. No
public export moved, so no consumer package owes a test here.

**Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived
**61 families** from this diff; all 61 ran, **all exit 0**, reconciled with `--ran` carrying each
exit code — "61 derived, 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". Three of them
(`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`) first exited 3
`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, were given the repo-wide build CI gives them, and then exited 0; the exit-3
runs are recorded as not-measured rather than as failures. Re-derived after `git fetch origin main`:
identical list. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` ran **unnarrowed** (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0.

**Changeset — measured, not assumed.** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is `private: false` with
`files: ["dist", …]`, and the edited symbol ships: `deleteManyData` occurs 5 times in
`packages/metadata-protocol/dist/index.js` against a negative control that occurs 0 times. So a
changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` does not apply. **`patch`**: a released package's bug fix,
and the published accept set does not move — no key added or removed, no request shape touched,
`errors` was already optional. What changes is the VALUE of an existing key, pulled back to what
`BatchOperationResultSchema.success` already declares. Hence `Clause-②: no`.

## Acceptance notes

Noticed while measuring, deliberately **not** carried here:

- **`batchData`'s `delete` arm carries the identical literal** — `protocol.ts:12543`, whose own
  comment calls it "the OTHER by-id bulk delete, ten lines from it": same
  `if (deleted === false) throw` followed by `results.push({ id: record.id, success: true, index })`.
  It is the same defect family on a third door (`POST /data/{object}/batch`). Not carried here: this
  card names `deleteManyData` and nothing else, and `protocol.ts` is held by another open claim, so
  the in-place exemption does not apply. Reported for filing.
- **Whether a surviving row deserves a per-row error code.** `ROLLED_BACK` / `NOT_ATTEMPTED` show the
  batch surface's own idiom is a ledger-registered code at HTTP 200; "matched and deliberately not
  deleted" has none, and a caller branching on `errors[0].code` therefore reads this row by the
  ABSENCE of `errors`. Minting one is a `packages/spec` widening — spec lane, not this PR.
- **`os data delete`'s unconditional `Record deleted: {id}` print** was already recorded on PR #19411
  and is not re-reported here.
- #19306 is not addressed here; PR #19411 remains open on the same file, in a region this branch does
  not touch (`:11411`–`:11440` vs this card's `:13026`–`:13098`).
